title_en: Great Poems and Songs (3/20): Wang Wei and the Red Beans of Longing
note_en: To say "just as A is X," Chinese wraps the comparison in 就像……一样: 就像李白被称为"诗仙"……一样 "just as Li Bai is called the 'Immortal of Poetry.'" English needs only "just as" or "like," but Chinese usually closes the frame with 一样 at the end. The same pair works for simple comparisons too: 像风一样自由 "as free as the wind."
